name: Chungudi Jhola (Prawn Curry)
instructions: 1. Marinate the cleaned prawns with a pinch of salt and turmeric.
2. Heat mustard oil in a pan and lightly fry the prawns for 1-2 minutes; remove and set aside.
3. In the same oil, fry the potato cubes until golden brown and remove.
4. Add bay leaf to the remaining oil, then sauté onions until translucent.
5. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until the raw smell disappears.
6. Add tomatoes, turmeric, chili powder, cumin, and coriander powder; cook until oil separates.
7. Add the fried potatoes and prawns, stirring well to coat with the masala.
8. Pour in enough water to form a gravy, cover, and simmer until potatoes are cooked.
9. Finish with a sprinkle of garam masala and fresh coriander before serving.
description: Chungudi Jhola is a quintessential Odia delicacy, reflecting the state's deep coastal connection. Traditionally prepared with mustard oil and tempered with aromatic spices, this curry is a staple in Odia households, often enjoyed with steamed rice during festive occasions and daily meals.
